title: Champagne news-letters to Nevers 1590-91 and Laurière to Nevers 1593, BnF fr. 3623 and fr. 3625 (catalogue item 30)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's nevers.htm and GL.htm, DECODE list for fr. 3623/3625; no prior reading; DECODE gives folios.
Gallica thumbnails of both volumes; contact sheets; full-resolution pages of ff. 35-41, 88, 111 (fr. 3623) and ff. 10, 16 (fr. 3625).
No. 23: key slip on f. 36r transcribed; every code number in the letter resolves.
Tomokiyo's no. 46 (targets/nevers1593/key46.txt) tried on no. 24's figures: values do not fit.
Twelve two-digit runs of nos. 24, 25, 60 transcribed with the faint interlinear letters.
Interlinear glosses (Ludovic, union, a, n) give anchors; the values rise with the alphabet.
Alphabetical slots fill the table: la ligue, de la defiance du [17], de Chazeron, service read; two no. 24 runs stay open.
Search for fr. 3625 no. 55 across canvases 13-64 and 81-200: not found; no. 10 found at f. 10r with interlinear decipherment.
OAI item list of fr. 3625 matched to folios (no. 49 = f. 61, dated 3 not 9 July); no. 55 found at f. 66r, canvas 143; canvases 65-80 and 201-270 looked over.
No. 55 transcribed (8 runs, 86 groups); first three runs of no. 10 aligned with their interlinear decipherment.
Groups shared with no. 10's glossed runs read in no. 55: que le Roy soit encores, la volonte du pape, aussitost; about 15 of 86 groups.
All seven glossed runs of no. 10 aligned with their interlinear decipherment; 12-entry table (key_lauriere.txt), syllable groups not separable.
No. 55 read with the table: 19 of 86 groups; French LM not applicable to the syllabic remainder.

GitHub issue 13 (setsunaatto): Tomokiyo's Nevers key no. 57 (fr. 3995 ff. 102-103, 'Mons. de La Verriere', Chartres Feb 1593) is Lauriere's key; our 12-entry table is one group out of step. Tomokiyo's nevers.htm entry for no. 57 confirms the design and the writer.
Key sheet canvases 196-201 fetched; syllable rule (ba 1 be 15 bi 29 bo 43 bu 57), doubles 73-98 and every word code used in no. 55 checked on canvas 200; key57.txt written.

Issue's transcription of f. 66r lines 1-2 checked against the full-resolution page and our own ct_3625_55.txt: figures agree group for group. Issue's blind test on no. 10: 80% of glossed letters in runs >=4 vs shuffle max 30%.

No. 55 read in full with key no. 57 (reading_3625_55.txt): Henri IV's assembly, Lorraine's terms, the Pope's consent, Gondi for Tuscany; two letters missing in the cipher itself. key_lauriere.txt marked superseded.
Key no. 57 tried on no. 78's single group '96 □ 3 9̄ f 3': no sense.

Blind test of key no. 57 on no. 10 (f. 10r), contributed by setsunaatto in PR 15: five runs transcribed from crops that hide the office's interlinear decipherment, then scored against it (check_3625_10.py): 157 of 196 gloss letters fall in matching runs of 4 or more, against shuffled controls of at most 58 in 2000 (121/160 against at most 42 without L1, the run seen when the key was first applied).

No. 10's other eight glossed runs read with key no. 57 (transcribed with the glosses in view; 311/354 in matching runs of 4 or more) and 21 word numbers added to key57.txt from the sheet. Apart from spelling and gaps in the gloss, key and office disagree only in run R3: 'que [l'Espagne]' where the office wrote 'qui ne se', and 344 234 'tout hault' where it wrote 'pour son' (probably a slip for 334 'son').

PR 15 checked before merging: the script reproduces its table; our 21 Sept transcription of runs L1-L3 agrees with the blind one on every figure group but one; 18 of the 21 new word numbers, both duplicates (202, 320) and province 29 found on f. 103r; both header rows match the script's alphabet, which showed key57.txt had c and h reversed (corrected); swapping the e/i y-forms moves the blind score only from 157 to 152; the R3 figures 344 234 confirmed on f. 10r.

No. 10's one unglossed run transcribed from the page (U1 in ct_3625_10_rest.txt) and read: '[le grand duc de Toscane] quant [le Roy] nous bailla par escrit (sa?) volonté'; the barred 3 before 'volonté' is not on the sheet, 'sa' is a guess from context.

fr. 3985 located as Gallica btv1b90606498 (from targets/nevers1593/NOTES.md); IIIF manifest fetched; thumbnails of canvases 112-120 looked over: f. 58r = canvas 114 (Laverriere, Poissy, 12 Aug 1593), f. 58v = canvas 115 (address only); canvases 114, 115 and the key sheet fr. 3995 canvas 200 fetched at full size.
Tomokiyo nevers.htm no. 57 checked for a reading of f. 58: only the anchor phrase in a page-source comment, 17 9 70 26 17 32 a n s = 'de nature defians' and 304 = pour; no fuller reading.

Clear text and the two cipher runs (A: page lines 11-19; B: lines 21-24) transcribed from the deskewed canvas at 1.6-3x crops, with the office's interlinear decipherment as G lines (fr3985_f58/ct.txt, clear.txt). First crops followed the slope of the lines badly and paired cipher with the wrong gloss line; deskewing by 2.9 degrees fixed it.
Whole word list 99-353, the overbarred 200-203 and the province/town table of key no. 57 read off f. 103r (fr3985_f58/words57.tsv); key57.txt had only the words of nos. 10 and 55.

Key no. 57 applied unchanged (decode58.py): run A reads as French (prince de Conty, Madame d'Angouleme, Montmorency house, La Tremoille, 'de nature defians'); run B in part ('... du Pape pour atanter a la personne du [Cardinal de Bourbon]'). 222 of 248 cipher tokens read as sense (89.5%); fr-1600-letters -1.72 per char on the run A reading.

Run A checked word for word against the office's interlinear decipherment: agrees except A8 'a ceux' (office 'a cause'), A6 'eleoction' (office 'election'), A7 'gagnet' (office 'gagner'). Six writer's slips identified, each forced by context and the gloss (madame with 2 for 3; 44 for 40 in princi-; 334 for 335; 22 for 32 in fidelle; 57 without bar; 29-bar for vo).

Four name signs not on the f. 103r panel named from the gloss (prince de Conty, Messieurs de Montmorency, Cardinal de Bourbon; the B4 sign, gloss 'duc de Lorraine', not read). 183 'estre' + n t taken as 'estant' (the gloss).

Tried every value of the full word list on the open groups: '340 20 34 ye plus' gives 'tabour le liet' (gloss 'tabour le lieu') with no established sense; B2 '6 lam 344' gives 'la a tout' (gloss 'la plus...'); B4 '28 25 203' gives 'te que fait' (gloss 'pour mo... du duc de Lorraine'); overbarred 252 is not on the sheet as read. Not read.

Gallica info.json for fr. 3985 canvas 114: the maximum is the 4719 x 6676 image already used. Cipher block fetched again as nine lossless PNG regions, deskewed, autocontrast + unsharp mask (greyscale microfilm: channel separation not applicable).

Names panel f. 103v (fr. 3995 canvas 201) read at full resolution: prince de Conty, M. de Montmorency, Cardinal de Bourbon, duc de Lorraine all present; the four f. 58 name signs move from grade C (gloss) to H (key). Key header rows re-read: the writer's caret (p) is a tall lambda like his lam (a), and on the sheet the u sign (Vs) is a blotted scroll close to the b sign (xi).

Re-read of the open signs: A3 'caret sigma ddag plus' = port[ee] (grade I; office 'a m...'); beta in principall, zig in monsieur, lam in de la, lieu in A6; B1 29-bar = Espagnols; B3 252 = lettre (the clear 'avoir les lettres' agrees); B4 last sign = duc de Lorraine; B2 corrected to 6 lam 340. 235 of 248 tokens read as sense (94.8%; run A 98.2%).

340 re-read on a lossless crop of the sheet: 'taboure' (the office glossed 'tabour'); 'et [340] le lieu ou il le pourra mettre' wants 'trouver' but no reading of the sheet gives it. B2 '6 lam 340' and B4 '28 25 202' give no sense; A2 two signs, A4 three signs of 'ceste', B1 one sign stay illegible. Not settled.

Key no. 57 (words57.tsv and the row + 14 x vowel syllables) applied to the two-digit runs of nos. 24/25/60: no sense ('qui pi bo ni lo fi ...'), confirming a different system; those 41 open figures stay without key.

Nos. 24/25/60: unknown letter values bracketed between known neighbours by the alphabetical order (52 h-i, 62 l-n, 92 s-v, 94 u-v, 95 u-z), all 240 combinations scored with fr-1600-letters over the ten runs, codes left out (anneal_twodigit.py). Best 52 i, 62 n, 92 u/v, 95 y ('de Launan', '...audovic'); none verifies on a second occurrence (92's second occurrence gives 'le [99] y u a v [05] i s'). Not accepted; 63/104 unchanged.

Cotgrave 1611 (archive.org fre_b2062733) and Nicot 1606 (fre_b1887920) searched for tabourer: 'to drumme; to rap, knocke, or thumpe at a window, doore'; no sense fitting f. 58 'et [340] le lieu ou il le pourra mettre'.

Writer's-slip test: every key word one digit from 340, and from the B2/B4 groups, substituted. 348 voir (and 341 tenir) makes A6 grammatical ('et voir le lieu ou il le pourra mettre'), a conjecture not counted (the office read tabour; the figure is a clear 340). B2 '6 lam 340' and B4 '28 25 202' give no sense with any neighbour. The character LM does not separate the candidates.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 233 tokens, 94 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.94 per letter; random keys -3.058 (z 9.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.062 (mean -2.09, z 9.0); annealer on the real text -2.002. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.94; polyphony 0.0; 15 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.002

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The two-digit alphabet of fr. 3623 nos. 24/25/60 was rebuilt from a few interlinear glosses on nos. 25 and 60 plus its alphabetical order, and the no. 55 groups from the interlinear decipherment of Lauriere's letter no. 10 in the same volume fr. 3625; no. 23 reads with its own key slip bound in at f. 36r. Laurière's no. 55 was then read in full with his own key sheet (Tomokiyo's Nevers key no. 57, fr. 3995 ff. 102-103), identified by an outside contributor (issue 13) and checked here.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ct_3623_twodigit.txt 63 of 104 + ct_3625_55.txt 85 of 86 + ct_3623_78.txt 0 of 6 (29 Sept 2026) + fr3985_f58/ct.txt 235 of 248 (decode58.py, second pass 3 Oct 2026; 222 on 2 Oct): 383 of 444. No. 23 (all names in its key) and no. 10 (scored against its gloss by check_3625_10.py) not counted.
outcome.notes: No. 23 read in full from its key; nos. 24/25/60 about three quarters of runs read; no. 55 19 of 86 groups from no. 10's glosses; no. 78 open. fraction_read 0.45 is an estimate from the notes (cipher tokens: about 70 of 104 two-digit figures, 19 of 86 no. 55 groups, no. 23 codes all, no. 78 none), not a measurement. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.418 (was 0.45 estimated). codes_open = the word codes of the nos. 24/25/60 table (12 = de read; 16, 17, 19, 39, 89, 99 open); no. 55's syllabic groups (67 of 86 open) not counted there. 29 Sept 2026: no. 55 read in full with key no. 57 (issue 13); fraction 0.755. 2 Oct 2026: fr. 3985 f. 58 (Laverriere, Poissy, 12 Aug 1593; Tomokiyo's letter for key no. 57) deciphered with key no. 57, 222 of 248 tokens (89.5%); fraction 0.833. 3 Oct 2026: f. 58 second pass 235/248 (94.8%); fraction 0.863. 3 Oct third pass (two-digit bracketed search, dictionaries, slip test): no counted change.

gaps.item: Nos. 24/25/60 code numbers 12, 16, 17, 19, 39, 89, 99 and the plain numbers of no. 24 (22, 51, 84, 44)
gaps.detail: no key bound with these letters; the alphabetical two-digit table covers letters only

gaps.item: No. 24 two passages, first half of the no. 25 'qu'on dict' passage, the name in no. 60 ('de la V?an')
gaps.detail: values fall outside the anchored slots of the alphabetical table (30-39, 48, 92-99 uncertain); no gloss over them

gaps.item: No. 78 (f. 111r), one group of about six mixed signs
gaps.detail: a single group, probably a name, in a different mixed code

gaps.item: fr. 3985 f. 58: two signs in s..t (sait), three middle signs of c...e (ceste), the sign after 29-bar in B1 (6 tokens)
gaps.detail: not decided at Gallica's maximum resolution with lossless PNG regions and enhancement; needs a colour scan or the manuscript
key values certain on the sheet but give no sense; the office gloss does not resolve them

GitHub issue 13: identified key no. 57 as Laurière's and read no. 55 with it (transcription and reading)
PR 15: blind test of key no. 57 against the office's interlinear decipherment of no. 10
his entry for key no. 57 names fr. 3985 f. 58, then deciphered here with the key; anchor phrase

prior.where: no. 23 key slip bound with the letter (f. 36r); interlinear glosses in no. 25 and no. 60; for no. 55 the key sheet itself (fr. 3995 ff. 102-103), catalogued by Tomokiyo as Nevers key no. 57; for fr. 3985 f. 58 the office's interlinear decipherment on the leaf itself, and Tomokiyo's anchor phrase

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue task via a parent agent. No target-specific intervention recorded. 29 Sept 2026: the key identification for no. 55 came from an outside contributor (setsunaatto, GitHub issue 13); this session verified it against the key sheet and the page. 30 Sept 2026: the same contributor (working with Claude, by their account) added a blind test of the key on no. 10 (PR 15); this session reviewed it against the key sheet and the page and merged it.
